newsitem.title: UK: Mining community positive on Busang find but wary.
newsitem.headline: Mining community positive on Busang find but wary.

text.p: The international mining community are positive towards the huge Busang gold find in Indonesia but wary over how the government handled the deal between the participating mining firms, analysts said on Wednesday.

A top Indonesian mining official said on Tuesday Canadian gold giant Barrick Gold Corp and Bre-X Minerals Ltd finally agreed on a 22.5-67.5 split of Busang, estimated to contain at least 57 million ounces of gold.

The deal ended weeks of speculation on whether they could work together to develop one of the world's most glittering gold finds, estimated to be worth more than $21 million. Indonesia shares the remaining 10 percent of the find.
"I think that most people are quite positive about Busang itself. The deposit looks very good," said Roger Chaplin, an analyst from stockbrokers T.Hoare and Co.
"The problem is...on how the whole thing has been handled. It will make the exploration, mining company a little bit wary about how they do business in Indonesia," he added.

Indonesia has pressed Bre-X to strike a deal with Barrick, one of the world's biggest gold miners. Bre-X already has a work contract and a local partner for the Busang I area of the find, which contains only 2.6 milion ounces.
Chaplin said there was an open question why Indonesia did not allow Bre-X to open the bidding to other companies.
"Why Barrick?," asked Chaplin. "It's no doubt they have a good reputation, a good mining company. But why did the Indonesian government pick Barrick in particular," he said.

A source close to the negotiations between the two companies said in Jakarta on Tuesday the deal covered the Busang II and III areas of the find, which contain the bulk of the gold. The companies will later form a joint venture, opening way for contracts of work to further explore and develop the property, and to settle disputes with local partners.
The source said Bre-X also wanted to clarify with the Mines and Energy Ministry the procedures for a joint application with Barrick for a new contract of work for Busang II and III.
Chaplin said he believed the deal would value Bre-X at close to the current share price of between $20 and $21.
Despite the controversies, analysts are positive towards Busang's future.
An analyst who declined to be identified said Busang would yield a low cost production of about $120 an ounce.
"It will have a very low cost production of $120 an ounce and I think it will perform very well," he said.
He said Busang was expected to produce 2.62 million ounces of gold per year once production started in 2000.
The Busang gold find is located in Indonesia's East Kalimantan province on Borneo island. -- London Newsroom, + 44 171 542 8065
